review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: Include patient as a group/random effect and batch as a covariate where estimable.
errors.issue: MOFA grouping is not a generic mixed-model patient random intercept. Specify an actually supported paired model or justified preprocessing/downstream test; MEFISTO temporal covariates are a different model, not an interchangeable batch-adjustment switch.

errors.quote: Use Fisher, Stouffer, or joint pathway methods.
errors.issue: Standard Fisher/Stouffer combination requires attention to dependence across the same patients and shared annotations. Specify a dependence-aware implementation or calibrated joint null.

errors.quote: correlation of program scores with the discovery cohort
errors.issue: Independent cohorts contain different patients, so their sample score vectors cannot be directly correlated without correspondence. Compare paired effects/distributions or common-feature effects instead.

errors.quote: without bridging, QC drift correction, or external validation
errors.issue: Ordinary pooled-QC drift correction alone cannot identify a fully confounded biological contrast. Bridge actual pre/post specimens under a balanced design, or restrict inference; independent validation also needs its own identifiable design.
Enrichment can legitimately guide pathway-first discovery when selection and validation are handled honestly. The answer later partially recognizes this; do not impose an exclusive sequence.

errors.quote: For metabolites, paired t-tests, Wilcoxon tests, or mixed models are options.
errors.issue: The design lists multiple analysis alternatives but does not freeze a primary selection rule, complete scoring projection or missing-block rule. For an operational protocol, specify how the method is chosen within training data and how a new patient is scored.

rationale: Sound high-level pairing, batch warnings, nested selection and source-to-claim limits. It remains a menu rather than a fully specified pipeline, and several statistical/software instructions are not executable or calibrated as stated. Correct dependence, cross-cohort comparisons and the MOFA model specification.
reference_guardrails: All twelve complete received final answers, the exact question/packet and full reference answer were personally read. No API judge or hidden reasoning was used; no real pipeline execution was performed.

M2 states that most post-treatment metabolomics samples share one batch, but does not specify how pretreatment samples are distributed. Check patient/time/batch design rank, overlap and precision; concentration alone is not proof of complete confounding.
Different batches across RNA and protein do not imply independent artifacts. Shared samples, handling, composition and time-aligned allocation can create cross-layer concordance.

The reference recommends paired contrasts as integration input. Centered delta factors describe between-patient heterogeneity and need not retain a mean shift; one delta row per patient has no pre/post label to classify. A sample-level score or explicit retained mean-effect model is a valid alternative.

The reference rule rejecting batch- or donor-dominated factors is too categorical. Association/variance dominance is diagnostic, not proof of artifact. For one delta per patient, a separate fixed effect for each donor is not a meaningful factor-association test.

Pairing alone does not justify sign permutations. Require a suitable null symmetry/exchangeability model, address technical dependence and rerun selection. Joint row permutations leave unsupervised covariance unchanged.

External projection with frozen weights cannot validate those same weights by correlation. Independent cohorts do not supply matched patient-score vectors; compare a defined population-level endpoint.

Missing-view algorithms do not identify MNAR mechanisms. Missing-platform renormalization changes the score definition. Refit learned processing within training folds and predefine external score applicability.

The reference protocol says stop and restart if external data were used for tuning. Restarting on the same exposed cohort does not restore independence; a revised program requires a new untouched evaluation.

The reference power wording must include biological paired variation, design and multiplicity. Technical replicates alone do not estimate biological sampling variability, and no universal n cutoff is inferred from 30 patients.

Measured/testable enrichment universes, dependence-aware tests and frozen annotations matter; a ranked analysis of all filtered tested features can satisfy this without a mandatory keyword. Late integration and pathway-first discovery are valid alternatives.
Purity changes can be part of the treatment-associated specimen response. Adjusting a post-treatment variable changes the estimand and does not automatically prove or remove confounding.
Original frozen keys and candidates remain unchanged. Corrections are disclosed here; reviews are provisional, unblinded and not expert validation.
